title: Bangladeshi workers stranded in Sri Lanka after fake job offers
excerpt: A survivor-led group asks the Home Ministry to bring workers home, investigate brokers and treat them as possible trafficking victims.
content:
Bangladeshi workers promised jobs in Europe and elsewhere have been left stranded in Sri Lanka without food, housing or money, and a survivor-led group has asked the government to bring them home, The Business Standard reported on 17 November.

The workers were promised jobs in Europe, Serbia, Albania, Bosnia and Fiji, but were left in Colombo and Katunayake. The report describes them as "several" and does not give a number.

Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation sent a memorandum to the Home Ministry's senior secretary, with copies to the Foreign Ministry, the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry and the CID. It asks for the workers' return, an investigation of the brokers involved, and for returnees to be treated as possible trafficking victims rather than offenders. Md Al-Amin Noyon is the group's president.

Why it matters

Using third countries as transit points for fake overseas jobs is a known trafficking route. How returnees are treated decides whether they get support or face blame. Safe migration and anti-trafficking NGOs can help with screening, legal aid and reintegration.

What to watch

Whether the Bangladesh mission in Colombo moves to repatriate the workers, and whether the CID opens cases against the brokers.

Sources
